etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Bowdler +‎ -ize; named after English physician Thomas Bowdler (1754–1825). In 1818, he published a censored version of William Shakespeare (The Family Shakespeare), expurgating “those words and expressions […] which cannot with propriety be read aloud in a family.”
senses: (transitive) To remove or alter those parts of a text considered offensive, vulgar, or otherwise unseemly.
